aboon: above; a Scottish and archaic word meaning overhead or higher up
appellation: a name or title given to someone or something
ammunition: gunpowder, bullets, and other materials used in firing weapons
analogous: similar or comparable in some important respects to something else
ascribed: attributed or credited to a particular cause or person
assailed: attacked violently, either with blows or with harsh words
astonished: greatly amazed or surprised by something unexpected
barbarians: people regarded as uncivilized, primitive, or cruel by outsiders
betraying: revealing something secret or showing one's true feelings unintentionally
bosom: the chest or breast of a person, regarded as the seat of feeling
circumvolant: revolving or moving in a circle around something
cruisers: warships sent to patrol the seas and hunt enemy or illegal vessels
deposits: layers of material such as sand or mud left behind by water or wind
dread: deep fear or anxiety about something terrible that may happen
dye-stuffs: substances, plant or mineral, used to color cloth or other materials
dye-woods: woods from which coloring matter is extracted for dyeing cloth
execrations: curses or loud expressions of hatred and angry denunciation
fetishes: objects believed to hold magical or spiritual power, worshipped by some peoples
fetishman: a priest or magician who looks after and uses fetish objects
formations: natural arrangements or structures of rock, earth, or other material
fossil: the preserved remains or traces of ancient plants or animals in rock
geological: relating to the study of the earth's rocks, layers, and history
gratified: pleased or satisfied, especially by having a wish or desire fulfilled
gratings: iron bars or grates covering openings in a ship's deck for ventilation
heartless: cruel and unfeeling, showing no pity or compassion toward others
horizon: the line where the sky seems to meet the earth or sea
indefinite: not clearly fixed, limited, or determined in extent or time
insulated: isolated or cut off from contact with other places or people
alluvial: formed of soil, sand, or gravel deposited by flowing water
laborious: requiring great effort, hard work, and long exertion
lagoons: shallow pools of salt water separated from the open sea by sandbars
marshes: low, wet lands covered in water and soft mud
musket: an old type of long gun fired from the shoulder, used by soldiers
mutiny: an open rebellion of sailors or soldiers against their officers
navigators: people who plan and direct the course of a ship or aircraft
oatswain: a ship's officer in charge of sails, rigging, and deck crew (boatswain)
ostensibly: apparently or on the surface, though perhaps not in reality
piracies: criminal acts of robbery and attack committed at sea by pirates
precipices: steep cliffs or rock faces with an almost vertical drop
presumed: supposed or assumed to be true without full proof
procure: to obtain or acquire something, often with some effort
profusion: a large amount or abundance of something
reverence: deep respect mixed with awe, especially toward something sacred
rigging: the ropes, chains, and masts that support and control a ship's sails
sovereign: a supreme ruler, such as a king, queen, or emperor
squadron: a group of warships or aircraft organized as a single fighting unit
squalls: sudden, violent gusts of wind, often with rain or snow
surge: a large, powerful rush or swell of water, such as a big wave
tropic: the hot region of the earth lying near the equator
verdure: fresh green vegetation covering the land
vapor: moisture suspended in the air as mist, steam, or fog
villany: wicked or criminal behavior; an old spelling of villainy
wretched: miserable, unhappy, or very poor in condition or circumstances
wretchedness: great misery, poverty, or unhappiness suffered by people
zenith: the highest point reached in the sky directly above an observer
chiefly: mainly or most importantly; for the most part
mischief: harm, trouble, or damage caused by someone's playful or wicked acts
muzzle: the open front end of a gun barrel, or a device covering an animal's mouth
apprehend: to understand clearly, or to seize and arrest a person
rapidly: very quickly or at high speed
tongues: languages or dialects spoken by particular peoples
dialects: regional or local varieties of a language with distinct words or pronunciation
nation: a large group of people sharing a common territory, history, and government
